proof.criterion: Item 1. A claim relaunched into any pod other than the round's own takes no further part in that round: its part is frozen as the old pod left it, no ask of that round is re-sent into the new pod, and an answer from there is refused. The gone-pod report is the same whichever comes first, the relaunch or the ErrPodGone read.
proof.surface: The claim machines driven through their own death and relaunch (internal/supervise), and the daemon's sweep over a real PostgreSQL reading the report (internal/daemon).
proof.command: cd packages/daemon && go test ./internal/supervise -run 'TestPodUpdateAnUnansweredClaimRelaunchedIntoAnotherPodIsAskedNothingMore|TestPodUpdateAnAnsweredClaimRelaunchedIntoAnotherPodKeepsItsAnswer|TestPodUpdateAClaimInTheRoundsOwnPodStillLosesItsAnswerToAForeignTurn' -count=1; and the two report-level tests in ./internal/daemon.
proof.observed: All pass at the head. Both orders are covered at report level, which is what the architect asked for: relaunch-first by TestPodUpdateWritesOnTheIssueWhenThePodWentWithoutItsRound, which moves both claims into the replacement pod and then asserts the issue is written on exactly once, naming the round and the implementer that had not answered and NOT naming the tester that had, with no ReplacePod call; and gone-read-first by TestPodUpdateEndsTheRoundAtTheFirstReadOfAGonePod. The 'answer in the new pod changes nothing' and 'no ask re-sent there' clauses are pinned by the two supervise tests.
proof.negativeControl: In-tree, with Claim.leftPodRound forced to return false: TestPodUpdateAnUnansweredClaimRelaunchedIntoAnotherPodIsAskedNothingMore fails 'prompts sent = 2' -- the round's own ask re-sent into the new pod under the same delivery id -- and TestPodUpdateAnAnsweredClaimRelaunchedIntoAnotherPodKeepsItsAnswer fails with the answer withdrawn. The control TestPodUpdateAClaimInTheRoundsOwnPodStillLosesItsAnswerToAForeignTurn PASSES in the same run, which is what says the guard is not too wide.

proof.criterion: Item 2, checked hardest as the architect directed because it was first a subagent's unverified work on the wip branch. A round ends only by replacing its pod or because that pod is gone: when no live claim records the round's pod, the sweep asks the runtime about the pod itself and ends only on runtime.ErrPodGone.
proof.surface: The daemon's sweep over a real PostgreSQL with real claim machines, driven through the operator's suspension (which clears the locator) landing between the tick's snapshot and the live read, and through the resume back into the same pod.

The first: nothing replaced, no 'the pod is replaced and the round is over' line, the round and the answer still on the claim, and the operator's resume lets the next sweep replace the pod. The second: the round ends through endRoundOverAGonePod exactly once with no ReplacePod call.
